name: Shackleton Crater
terrain: Impact crater depression and permanently shadowed polar floor
slope: 25° - 34° (Steep inner crater walls and rim crest)
temperature: -233°C to -53°C (Cryogenic cold traps 40 K to 220 K)
geology: Anorthositic impact breccia, trapped volatile ice, shattered regolith
surface_conditions: Cryogenic frost regolith, deep shadows, perpetual darkness on crater floor
volatiles: Trapped volatile ice candidates in cryogenic depressions
sunlight: High continuous illumination on ridge peaks (>85% annual)

name: Marius Hills / Oceanus Procellarum
terrain: Basaltic mare plain with collapsed volcanic lava tube skylights
terrain_type: Basaltic Lunar Mare & Subterranean Lava Tubes
slope: 2° - 15° (Flat mare plain with abrupt collapse pit walls)
temperature: -173°C to 117°C (Wide lunar day/night swing; subterranean stable ~ -20°C)
geology: Titanium-rich flood basalts, olivine-pyroxene lava tubes, pyrometasomatic minerals
surface_conditions: Fine cohesive regolith dust on surface; boulder rubble in cave skylights
radiation_level: High on surface; Low within collapsed skylight tubes
volatiles: Extremely dry; trace solar wind implanted hydrogen

name: Schrödinger Basin
terrain: Complex multi-ring impact basin and pyroclastic volcanic vents
slope: 5° - 28° (Peak ring mountains, graben faults, and rim scarps)
geology: Deep lunar mantle uplift, impact melt sheets, explosive volcanic glass beads
surface_conditions: Fractured bedrock blocks, dark pyroclastic ash blankets, impact craters
volatiles: Pyroclastic volcanic glass vents & deep crustal exposures
sunlight: Long shadows with periodic rim illumination

name: Jezero Crater
terrain: Ancient dried paleolake basin, fluvial fan delta, and crater floor
slope: 1° - 12° (Gentle sedimentary delta deposits to crater rim edges)
temperature: -133°C to 17°C (140 K to 290 K diurnal swing)
geology: Hydrated smectite clays, carbonates, iron-magnesium silicates, lacustrine mudstones
surface_conditions: Fine oxidized red dust, wind-sculpted ripples, boulder fields, fractured mudstone

name: Olympus Mons Aureole & Slopes
terrain: Massive basaltic shield volcano flanks, aureole deposits, and caldera scarps
terrain_type: Massive Shield Volcano Basaltic Flows & Scarp
slope: 4° - 35° (Gentle lower shield slopes with sheer perimeter scarps up to 8 km)
temperature: -123°C to -23°C (150 K to 250 K; thin atmospheric column)
geology: Tholeiitic basalt flows, volcanic ash, lava channels, collapsed pits
surface_conditions: Abrasive vesicular basalt lava fields, windblown dust drifts, steep scarp rubble
volatiles: Desiccated basalt; scoria and ash fields
sunlight: High incident solar flux (above lower dust haze layer)

name: Valles Marineris (Candor Chasma)
terrain: Massive tectonic rift canyon system, layered plateaus, and landslide chasms
terrain_type: Massive Tectonic Rift & Layered Sulfate Deposits
slope: 5° - 42° (Flat canyon valley floors with towering sheer cliff scarps)
temperature: -113°C to 22°C (160 K to 295 K; denser local canyon microclimate)
geology: Layered sulfate deposits, kieserite, hematite, volcanic ash strata, basalt
aridity: Hyper-arid desert canyon (localized morning water ice fog)
surface_conditions: Tectonic talus rubble, high-contrast iron-oxide walls, sand dune fields
volatiles: Hydrated sulfate minerals & canyon wall scree
